claims: Because the classroom teacher scale runs through the 30% and 37% brackets, the saving is meaningful at the top of the scale and smaller at the graduate step.
whys: The 37% bracket starts above $135,000 (tax-rates-reference.ts line 145). The top of the classroom scale is below that in 7 of 8 states: NSW 133,422, VIC 118,063, QLD 119,357, WA 127,737, SA 123,236, TAS 122,393, ACT 129,106. Only NT (136,997) reaches 37%. On 7 pages the graduate and top steps sit in the same 30% bracket, so the per-dollar saving is the same at both ends. The 30% and 37% figures are also typed into the template, not taken from constants.
constants: lib/constants/tax-rates-reference.ts (brackets) with topOfClassroomScale() from lib/data/teacher-pay; the sentence should be generated for each state
reviewerNotes: Verified the writer's 37% bracket question with tsx on lib/data/teacher-pay. topOfClassroomScale gives NSW 133422, VIC 118063, QLD 119357, WA 127737, SA 123236, TAS 122393, ACT 129106, NT 136997. The 37% bracket starts above 135,000, so only the NT top step reaches it. On 7 of 8 pages, 'runs through the 30% and 37% brackets' and 'saving is meaningful at the top ... smaller at the graduate step' are wrong, because both ends of the scale are in the 30% bracket. This needs a per-state template fix, not a prose edit.

The state's own progression data partly contradicts it: NT 'One increment every 12 months, and it is hard to withhold', WA 'An annual increment to 2.9', VIC 'Progression happens once a year, on 1 May'. It holds for NSW (accreditation gate) and SA (207 duty days). For NT it reads as wrong.
